source.title: On open problems in polling systems

accepted.question_text: Consider a two-queue cyclic polling system in steady state with one server that visits Q1 and Q2 in order, independent Poisson arrivals to queue Qi at rate λi, independent service times Bi, and independent switch-over times between queues. Queue Q1 uses gated service, meaning that during a visit to Q1 the server serves exactly those customers present at the start of that visit, while queue Q2 uses 1-limited service, meaning that during a visit to Q2 the server serves at most one customer if one is present. Determine the joint probability generating function of the queue-length vector at polling instants for this G/1-L system.
accepted.context_brief: Two-queue polling system with gated and 1-limited service

evidence.quote: In the present paper (and in almost the whole polling literature), the server visits the N queues in cyclic order Q1, Q2, . . . , QN , Q1, . . . , and the arrival processes of customers at the various queues are assumed to be independent Poisson processes, with rate λi at Qi , i = 1, . . . , N. The service requirements at Qi , denoted by Bi , are independent, identically distributed random variables

The three most important service disciplines are exhaustive (E): a queues is served until it is empty; gated (G): the server only serves those customers which were present at the start of the visit; and 1-limited (1-L): the server serves only one customer – if any is present.
Open problem 1. Determine the joint queue-length PGF at polling instants in the two-queue G/1-L polling system.

accepted.question_text: Consider a cyclic polling system with finitely many queues, deterministic switch-over times between successive queues, and general renewal arrival processes at the queues. The source conjectures that, when the deterministic switch-over times tend to infinity, the polling system converges to a deterministic cyclic system. Provide a rigorous proof of that conjecture.
accepted.context_brief: Renewal-arrival polling systems with large deterministic switch-over times

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2. A cyclic polling system with general (renewal) arrival processes converges to a deterministic cyclic system when the deterministic switch-over times tend to infinity.

Open problem 2. Provide a rigourous proof of Conjecture 4.2, which states that a cyclic polling system with general (renewal) arrival processes converges to a deterministic cyclic system when the deterministic switch-over times tend to infinity.

accepted.question_text: Identify and classify which polling systems, in terms of their service disciplines, visit disciplines, and scheduling disciplines, exhibit the limiting behaviour discussed in the paper: namely, convergence to deterministic behaviour under large switch-over times, including settings such as systems with dynamic visit orders where the server need not follow a pre-determined queue order.
accepted.context_brief: Classification of polling disciplines with deterministic large-switch-over limits

evidence.quote: [14] shows via numerical testing that similar limit theorems as presented here carry over to systems with Poisson arrivals and dynamic visit orders (i.e., there exists no pre-determined order in which the queues are served).
A resulting open problem is, therefore, the classification of polling systems in terms of service, visit and scheduling disciplines, which exhibit the discussed behaviour.
